messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-9321 — inference-api-prod high error rate (>8% 5m). Trigger: 5xx spike on /v1/generate. Severity: P1. Links: https://pagerduty.example/INC-9321, runbook: https://confluence.example/runbooks/inference-api-prod

jordan: oncall here, picking up. checking metrics now.

jordan: @pagerduty-bot ack INC-9321

pagerduty-bot: Jordan acknowledged INC-9321 (on-call). Escalation timers suspended.

leah: seeing similar 5xxs from eu-west cluster in logs — large payloads with long prompts? throwing OOMs / kv cache errors. adding logs: 
```
2026-03-14T02:07:12Z inference-runtime ERROR shard-12: allocate_kv_cache failed: cudaOOM
2026-03-14T02:07:13Z inference-runtime WARN request 0x7f3e: response truncated
```

jordan: thanks. I'm rolling back the new routing rule we shipped at 02:00 that allowed 1M token prefixes for some customers. Suspect kernel/kv-cache regression.

niya: I'm the secondary on-call, got auto-escalation notice earlier — saw the initial page didn't get immediate ack for ~2m and PD escalated to me, but jordan acked now. Are you planning to fallback?

jordan: planning to toggle fallback to smaller-kv-profile and scale replica count for the affected pool. Doing canary on one node first.

ashok: Manager escalation also fired because policy hit manager after 5m unacked. I'm here to support customer comms and prioritization. Which customers are affected?

leah: quick query shows spike from two enterprise tenants: tenant-42 (low-volume long-context) and tenant-88 (batch infer). Impact: ~1200 failed requests in last 5m, about 0.6% of overall traffic but concentrated in those tenants — likely user-visible errors for some customers.

jordan: executing remediation steps from runbook: 
1) reroute tenant-88 to fallback model (v1-small-kv)
2) reduce max_prefix_tokens to 256 for risky requests
3) scale pool inference-prod-01 +2 replicas

jordan: running command to update routing rule: 
```
# update route for tenant-88
redwoodctl routes set tenant-88 --model v1-small-kv --weight 1 --force
```

incident-bot: redeploy job started: rollout/route-update-tenant-88 (ci-2981). Watch: https://ci.example/builds/ci-2981

niya: I'm applying quota-limit patch for large prompts as well (`max_prefix_tokens: 256`) — pushing config to canary.

leah: logs after reroute show drop in 5xx for tenant-88 but tenant-42 still spiking. Looks like tenant-42 uses very long prefixes that trigger the kernel regression.

jordan: for tenant-42 let's enable synchronous fallback to hosted-legacy runtime (slower but stable) while we investigate. Updating routing to split 50/50.

ashok: I'll prepare a short customer note and ask Support to notify tenant-42 and tenant-88. @leah can you estimate ETA for full rollback?

leah: rollback of the routing rule should be complete in ~10m once canary is healthy. Kernel hotfix investigation ongoing (eng-runtime team looped).

pagerduty-bot: INC-9321 escalated to secondary (niya) then manager (ashok) before primary acknowledgement window elapsed. Current status: acknowledged by jordan.

jordan: canary checks looking good — 5xx rate down to baseline on canary node. Proceeding to scale + propagate.

leah: scaling finished on pool inference-prod-01, replicas +2. Overall 5xx dropped to 0.5% and latency stabilized.

niya: since auto-escalation triggered, doc the timing for postmortem: pager fired at 02:06, primary ack at 02:09, secondary notify at 02:08, manager page at 02:12. Will include this in incident timeline.

ashok: agreed — capture who was paged and why. Support comms: I drafted a short message for tenant-42 and tenant-88. Jordan/leah please review: 
"We're investigating increased request failures on inference-api-prod affecting some long-context and batch jobs. We've applied temporary routing changes and fallbacks; full mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause."

jordan: LGTM. Send it out once you add contact for escalation.

leah: sent customer notes via support ticket #SUP-1209 and Slack channel #customer-tenant-42 with snippet.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC-9321 status updated: acknowledged -> resolved (automation) after remediation metrics sustained for 15m. Resolution link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-9321/resolve

jordan: resolving here after metrics stable and support notified. I'll open a postmortem ticket and assign owners for kernel regression and route guardrails.

niya: leaving a note for on-call handoff later: primary handled remediation but auto-escalation to secondary + manager happened because of initial delay — we should tighten escalation windows or increase latency of auto-escalation when primary likely to respond quickly.

ashok: agree — also action item: add explicit runbook step for forced fallback to hosted-legacy for long prefixes. I'm creating the task: https://tasks.example/TASK-489

leah: adding logs and traces to the incident ticket. Will include the KV cache OOM traces and the routing diff.

jordan: postmortem outline created: owner=jordan, detection timeline, mitigation steps, customer outreach, long-term fix (kernel/quantization patch), and runbook improvements. ETA draft: 2026-03-16 EOD.

leah: closing thread here for live mitigation notes. Follow-up postmortem in #postmortems once writeup done. :+1:
